html:
Hurricane David struck Dominica as a category 5 storm on 29 August 1979, less than a year after independence. It destroyed or damaged most homes and left much of the island's population homeless.

The storm wiped out the banana crop, the island's main export, and the forests. It then hit the Dominican Republic, where floods and landslides killed far more people, around two thousand.

The next year voters chose Eugenia Charles, the first woman prime minister in the Caribbean, to lead the rebuilding. In 2017 Hurricane Maria hit the island even harder, a few weeks after Irma had passed to the north.
